title: Performance Efficiency pillar (use resources well)
hook: Performance Efficiency means using computing resources efficiently and scaling to meet demand without over-provisioning. Right-size services, use managed offerings, and measure before optimizing.

blocks.text: Principles: democratize advanced technologies (managed services), go global in minutes, use serverless where fit, experiment often, and consider mechanical sympathy. Trade compute types (EC2, Fargate, Lambda), storage (EBS vs instance store vs S3), databases (RDS vs DynamoDB vs Aurora), caching (ElastiCache, CloudFront), and network paths.

entries.example: t3.medium not r6g.2xlarge for idle API

entries.plainDefinition: Lambda scales per invocation — no server management
Store hot data closer to consumers
Edge cache for static and dynamic content

blocks.text: Interviewers ask why DynamoDB over RDS, or when Lambda beats ECS. Performance pillar is about matching architecture to access patterns — not maximum raw speed.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: measure first, right-size, managed services, cache, global edge, match data store to access pattern.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Measure baseline
items.body: CloudWatch metrics, X-Ray traces, load tests define p50/p99 latency.

items.title: Select service type
items.body: Match compute and data store to access pattern and burst profile.

items.title: Add caching and CDN
items.body: Reduce origin load; tune TTL and cache keys.

items.title: Review and experiment
items.body: Load test after changes; remove over-provisioned resources.

snippet.label: DynamoDB on-demand
snippet.code:
OrdersTable:
  Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
  Properties:
    BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
    AttributeDefinitions:
      - AttributeName: pk
        AttributeType: S
    KeySchema:
      - AttributeName: pk
        KeyType: HASH
snippet.explanation: Scale throughput automatically for spiky SaaS workloads.

snippet.label: CloudFront cache policy
snippet.code:
CachePolicy:
  Type: AWS::CloudFront::CachePolicy
  Properties:
    CachePolicyConfig:
      DefaultTTL: 300
      MinTTL: 0
      MaxTTL: 3600
      ParametersInCacheKeyAndForwardedToOrigin:
        QueryStringsConfig:
          QueryStringBehavior: all
snippet.explanation: Edge caching reduces origin latency and load.

snippet.label: X-Ray trace summary
snippet.explanation: Find slow/faulty segments before guessing optimizations.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Oversized instances "for headroom" without metrics. Wrong database for access pattern (relational for key-value hot path). Caching without cache invalidation strategy.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: p99 latency SLO dashboards; cache hit ratio; Compute Optimizer savings applied; load test results before/after architecture change.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Optimizing code before measuring — rejected. Strong answer: baseline metrics, bottleneck identification, right service selection, then tune.

interviewTakeaways: Performance Efficiency = right resource types, scale to demand, measure before optimize.
Managed services and serverless reduce undifferentiated ops.
Cache and CDN are first-class — not afterthoughts.
60s: Measure p99, match compute/DB to pattern, cache at edge and app, right-size with Compute Optimizer. Mechanical sympathy for data stores.
Follow-up: when does Lambda cold start break your SLO?
commonPitfalls: Strong answer: X-Ray/latency baseline, bottleneck, then architectural fix.
Relational DB for pure key-value hot path without joins.

jsTsCorrelations.note: pg pool in Node prevents RDS connection exhaustion — performance at app layer.
Dynamic import() reduces Lambda bundle cold start — performance tradeoff.
